machine: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, archlinux:base-devel container, no GPU, cage on the wlroots headless backend with the pixman renderer

startup_seconds.note: Process start to the first buffer on the toplevel's surface, median of three launches. The three were 1.127, 0.690 and 0.668 s, the first paying for a cold page cache. The ceiling is about four times the median, which is what the startup probes in docs/development.md use, because a shared runner's speed is not its own.

startup_lived_in_seconds.note: PROVISIONAL, retaken before merge. Process start to the first buffer on the toplevel's surface with the lived-in profile, file-cache cold, median of three launches on the Lenovo: 1.265, 1.276 and 1.283 s.

memory_mebibytes.note: Proportional set size of the whole process tree, one Space, one page. The ceiling is twice the measurement, as the frozen-tab probe's is.

space_mebibytes.note: What each Space after the first adds, each holding the same page, averaged over four Spaces. The run was 482.7, 659.8, 682.0 and 705.2 MiB: the second Space costs the engine a set of processes the rest then share, so the average is above the 23 MiB each later Space added. The ceiling is twice the average.

frozen_growth_mebibytes.note: What an away Space's page goes on taking once frozen, over ten seconds, against ADR 0033. It is read from the engine's processes, the browser's own left out, because on CI the browser process takes a step of about 6 MiB at no predictable moment (#467). Tighter than the others on purpose: the same page grew 30.1 MiB in the six seconds it was on show, a page left running while away is throttled to a megabyte a second and added 10.04 MiB here with Freezing switched off, and a reading's own noise is a tenth of a megabyte.

pageload_fresh_hosts_milliseconds.note: What Content blocking adds to a page of 40 images from 40 hosts it has never seen, the median with blocking on minus the median with the site switched off, ten loads each: 151.5 ms against 133.3 ms. Measured on 2026-09-28 against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, so this holds CNAME uncloaking's lookups as well as the rule check, the Refusal tally and the refused-request list. Secure DNS off. The hosts resolve through dnsmasq on the container's resolver, with CNAME chains, not host-resolver rules. Procedural cosmetic filtering is measured separately under #402. The ceiling is four times the difference. Two loads the engine cut short were repeated and not counted. On Arch's qt6-webengine, where uncloaking is compiled out, the same page added 6.1 ms (#371), so uncloaking's lookups are most of the difference.

pageload_known_hosts_milliseconds.note: The same for 40 images from 4 hosts resolved on the warm-up loads: 148.2 ms against 144.2 ms. Measured on 2026-09-28 against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, so this holds CNAME uncloaking's lookups as well as the rule check, the Refusal tally and the refused-request list. Secure DNS off. The hosts resolve through dnsmasq on the container's resolver, with CNAME chains, not host-resolver rules. Procedural cosmetic filtering is measured separately under #402. Four times the difference is 16 ms, under the 20 ms floor, because a shared runner's noise is bigger than a difference this small.

pageload_procedural_hosts_milliseconds.note: The common case with a page that procedural cosmetic rules are written against (ADR 0052): the markup and rules of tests/content-blocking/procedural-rules.json, one rule per operator and action, for both page hosts: 146.6 ms against 144.6 ms. The common case in the same run added 4.0 ms, so what the rules add over it is below what the runner can tell apart. Measured on 2026-09-28 against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, so this holds CNAME uncloaking's lookups as well as the rule check, the Refusal tally and the refused-request list. Secure DNS off. The hosts resolve through dnsmasq on the container's resolver, with CNAME chains, not host-resolver rules. Four times the difference is 8 ms, under the 20 ms floor.

first_contentful_paint_fresh_hosts_milli.note: How soon the page of 40 images from 40 hosts it has never seen first paints, blocking on, the median of ten loads. Measured on 2026-10-05 against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, with the page-load step's DNS setup, loads and spares. The page's own first-contentful-paint entry, from the navigation starting to the first frame that drew one of its images, under cage's pixman renderer and Chromium's software rasteriser. Two runs on CI's runner: a median of 62.0 ms (loads from 44.0 to 96.0 ms) and of 94.0 ms (64.0 to 112.0 ms), so the runner alone moved the median by half. The ceiling is four times the slower median, rounded up to ten milliseconds, as the startup and page-load ceilings are.

first_contentful_paint_known_hosts_milli.note: The same for the page of 40 images from 4 hosts resolved on the warm-up loads. Measured on 2026-10-05 against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, with the page-load step's DNS setup, loads and spares. The page's own first-contentful-paint entry, from the navigation starting to the first frame that drew one of its images, under cage's pixman renderer and Chromium's software rasteriser. Two runs on CI's runner: a median of 46.0 ms (44.0 to 80.0 ms) and of 60.0 ms (44.0 to 104.0 ms). The ceiling is four times the slower median.

live_tab_at_20_mebibytes.note: What each tab past its Space's first adds with 20 tabs across five Spaces, four in each: the tree at 20 less the tree with five Spaces and one tab each, over 15. Measured on 2026-10-05 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, one run (37360227439): 674.5 MiB with five Spaces open and one tab in each, 955.1 MiB with 20 tabs and 1514.1 MiB with 50. The ceiling is about twice the measurement, as the memory ceilings are.

live_tab_at_50_mebibytes.note: The same at 50 tabs, ten in each Space, over 45. Measured on 2026-10-05 on CI's runner against Omaweb's engine, omaweb-qtwebengine 6.11.2-3, one run (37360227439): 674.5 MiB with five Spaces open and one tab in each, 955.1 MiB with 20 tabs and 1514.1 MiB with 50. A tab costs the same at 50 as at 20, so the ceiling is the same, about twice the measurement.

live_tabs_idle_cpu_percent.note: The process tree's CPU over 30 s left alone with 50 tabs open, as a share of one core, the CPU of reaped children counted through their parents. In the same run the tree used 0.09 CPU s, no process more than 0.02 s, and no process ended. The ceiling is 2%, about seven times the measurement, because a share this small moves with whatever else the runner is doing.
